name: Indian Springs State Park
dates: Year round, beach Memorial Day to Labor Day
unique: The oldest state park in Georgia and arguably the oldest in the country, built around an artesian spring the Muscogee considered healing, with a stone spring house where you can still fill jugs for free.
buzz: People drive out with a dozen gallon jugs for the sulfur water, which says everything about how seriously this spring is taken locally. The lake beach and campground fill on summer weekends.

name: Dauset Trails Nature Center
unique: A privately funded nature center on more than a thousand acres with rehabilitated raptors, otters and deer along a walkable animal trail, plus mountain bike and hiking miles that connect into the surrounding wildlife management area.
buzz: Free, well kept and never crowded. Locals call it the best family afternoon in the county and bikers treat the trails as a secret worth keeping.

name: Indian Springs Holiness Camp Meeting
customer: Church groups, history curious travellers, singers
unique: A 140 acre camp meeting ground in continuous use since 1890, packed with wooden cottages and a great open tabernacle where families have come back to the same benches for five generations.
buzz: The singing is the draw, and visitors are welcome to sit in the back. People describe the grounds as a functioning nineteenth century village that happens to hold church for ten days a year.

name: The Village at Indian Springs
dates: Year round, some shops closed early in the week
customer: Day trippers, shoppers, people staying near the park
unique: A cluster of restored buildings across from the state park holding a bakery, a cafe, a quilt shop and a small inn, built to give the spring crowd somewhere to eat and stay.
buzz: The bakery and the porch sitting get the praise. It is small, and that is the point.

name: Fresh Air Bar-B-Que
dates: Tuesday to Saturday, lunch and early dinner
customer: Barbecue pilgrims, families, people off I-75
unique: Pit cooked pork over hickory in the same building since 1929, which the family says makes it the oldest barbecue restaurant in Georgia still at its original address, sliced or chopped and served on white bread.
buzz: The vinegar and pepper sauce and the pork skin are what people argue about. The pitmaster has been inducted into the American Royal Barbecue Hall of Fame, and the room has not changed.

name: Barnesville Buggy Days
unique: A whole weekend built on the fact that Barnesville once made more buggies than anywhere in the South, with a parade, crafts, a pageant and buggy exhibits in the downtown streets.
buzz: Fifty years in and still run by the town. The parade and the food lines are the local measure of a good September.

name: Old Jail Archives and Museum
unique: The county's old jail turned into an archive and museum by the historical society, with cell blocks still in place and the deed books and photographs that answer most questions about a Lamar County family.
buzz: Run by volunteers who will pull a file for you if you ask. The cells are the part kids remember.

name: Barnesville Depot
unique: The town's National Register railroad depot, the building that made Barnesville a cotton shipping point and then a buggy manufacturing town, standing at the head of the brick downtown.
buzz: A quick look on a downtown walk. Pair it with the square and the old jail.

name: Big Chic
unique: A counter service fried chicken stand on Forsyth Street that grew into a small Georgia chain, still selling the same pressure fried chicken and white bread the town grew up on.
buzz: Locals rank it against every chain in the state and pick this one. Cheap, fast and busy at noon.

name: Pike County Courthouse
unique: An 1895 courthouse on the square in Zebulon, on the National Register, with the original courtroom upstairs and a Main Street that still ends at the courthouse door.
buzz: The square is the whole town and it works. Come on a weekday and the upstairs courtroom is usually open.

name: Pike Pathways Heritage Tour
customer: Self guided road trippers, history people
unique: A free phone app tour of twenty places across Pike County, running from the Zebulon square out through Williamson, Meansville, Molena and Concord, with the history of each stop read aloud as you drive.
buzz: The kind of small county project that usually dies unnoticed. It works, it is free, and it turns a county of four small towns into an afternoon.

name: Meriwether-Pike Scenic Byway
unique: A 55 mile designated route through the two counties that ties the Roosevelt legacy at Warm Springs to the farms and crossroads towns in between, on two lane roads with no traffic and no billboards.
buzz: Drivers rate it as one of the prettier unheralded byways in the state, best in October when the cotton is in and the hardwoods turn.

name: The Oink Joint BBQ
dates: Lunch and early dinner, closed Sunday
unique: A barbecue shack in Zebulon that has become the de facto town lunchroom, with smoked pork and ribs and a handful of tables near the square.
buzz: Consistently the top rated place in town. Nothing fancy, and the pulled pork does what it should.

name: Doc Holliday Festival
unique: A one day festival in Griffin City Park for the town's most famous native son, a dentist who left Georgia for the Arizona Territory and ended up at the O.K. Corral, with reenactors, music and a lookalike contest.
buzz: Small and genuinely fun. The reenactment is the reason people come back, and the Tombstone cosplay is taken seriously.

name: Griffin Film and TV Marker Tour
customer: Film people, Walking Dead fans, downtown walkers
unique: A self guided marker trail through downtown Griffin covering more than a hundred films and shows shot here, from Fried Green Tomatoes to The Walking Dead, with the actual storefronts and courthouse steps on the route.
buzz: Fans of the shows treat it as a pilgrimage and the markers are genuinely informative. Pick up the list at the chamber and walk it in an afternoon.

name: Bailey-Tebault House
unique: A Greek Revival house on Meriwether Street kept by a historical society founded in 1969, with the parlors, documents and photographs that explain how a railroad town of 1840 became an industrial city.
buzz: Open for tours and events rather than on a fixed daily schedule, so call the society. The house itself is the best surviving answer to what Griffin looked like before the mills.

name: Wyomia Tyus Olympic Park
unique: A county sports park named for Griffin's Wyomia Tyus, the first person to win the Olympic 100 meters twice, with a trail called Ernie's Trail running through the woods beside the fields.
buzz: The name is the story and most visitors have no idea. The trail is short, shaded and quiet even when the tournaments are on.

name: Sprewell Bluff Park
unique: Thirteen hundred acres and three miles of frontage on the Flint, one of the longest undammed rivers in the east, with a bluff of exposed crystalline rock that geologists come from other states to read.
buzz: The view from the bluff is the photograph everybody takes. Paddlers put in here for the shoals, and the park stays quiet because almost nobody knows it exists.

name: Auchumpkee Creek Covered Bridge
unique: A lattice truss covered bridge built in 1892 by Herring and Alford, wrecked by the 1994 flood and rebuilt on the original stone piers, sitting on a dirt road over Auchumpkee Creek.
buzz: It is one of a handful of Georgia covered bridges you can still drive across. Photographers come for the morning light on the red siding, and the 1994 flood story comes with it.

name: Upson Historical Society
unique: A county historical society on South Church Street with a permanent exhibit on Thomaston during the Second World War, built around the mills, the bonds and the men who left, plus the files behind it.
buzz: Run by people who know the county cold and will find your family if you ask. Hours are short, so go early in the week.
